**Pick a power bank under 100 Wh.** That's the FAA's limit for spare lithium-ion batteries, and it's what nearly every airline follows. Two options fit:

**Best overall: Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W), $89.99**
- At about 74 Wh, it's under the 100 Wh limit.
- Its 100 W USB-C output can charge a laptop and a phone.
- It has 2 USB-C and 2 USB-A ports, and a full recharge takes about 1.5 hours.
- It weighs about 451 g (roughly 1 lb).
- No discount code worked when it was tested today.
- [Buy the Baseus Blade H1](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah)

**Best for iPhone users: Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10,000 mAh, 45 W), $53.99 with code AM52**
- At about 37 Wh, it's well under the limit.
- It has magnetic Qi2.2 wireless charging at 25 W for iPhone 16 and 17 (not the 16e). iPhone 12 to 15 get 15 W.
- It also charges over USB-C at 45 W.
- The list price is $59.99, and the code takes $6 off (tested in Baseus's cart on 2026-10-24).
- [Buy the Baseus PicoGo AM52](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w)

These are affiliate links, so Dealectric gets paid if you buy. The comparison comes from a single retailer-affiliated source, and it only lists each bank's watt-hours and carry-on status. It doesn't cover specific airline rules. I didn't find independent testing in these results.

**Rules for flying with any power bank**
- **Carry-on only.** The FAA says power banks can't go in checked bags. If your carry-on is gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **100 Wh limit.** Two larger batteries (101-160 Wh) are allowed with airline approval. Anything over 160 Wh is not allowed. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))
- **Protect the terminals.** Keep it in its original packaging, a pouch, or a case, or tape over the ports. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7), [IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/))
- **Airlines can be stricter.** Southwest, for example, has limited each passenger to one power bank since April 20, 2026. It must stay under the seat in front of you, not in the overhead bin. You can't charge it from in-seat power, and it must be visible while in use. ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)) Check your own airline's policy before you fly.
- **Don't fly with a damaged or recalled battery.** Tell the crew right away if one gets hot, swells, or smokes.

If you tell me your airline and what you need to charge (phone, laptop, or both), I can narrow it down.
